title: Degree-zero flat base change
statement: Let $f:X\to S$, $g:T\to S$, $h:Y\to X$ and $e:Y\to T$ form a Cartesian base-change square with $Y\cong X\times_ST$ [sbc-def-base-change-square]. Assume $f$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and its fibres over all points of $S$ are geometrically reduced over their residue fields [def-pc-scheme-fibre; def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. For every sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$ on $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets], the canonical base-change morphism $\beta_{\mathcal F}:f^{-1}g_*\mathcal F\longrightarrow h_*e^{-1}\mathcal F$ is an isomorphism. The inverse images and their composition and unit maps are those of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units]; direct image is evaluation on base-changed etale objects as in [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-continuous]. Explicitly, $\beta_{\mathcal F}$ is the adjoint transpose under $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ of $g_*\mathcal F\to g_*e_*e^{-1}\mathcal F\cong f_*h_*e^{-1}\mathcal F$, using the unit for $e$ and the Cartesian identification. In particular this holds when $f$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. There is no restriction on $g$ and no torsion hypothesis.

proof.text: For any object $j:U_0\to X$ of $X_{\Et}$, $j$ is flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. The composite $f\circ j$ is flat by [lem-pc-flat-compose]. It is locally of finite presentation: on affine neighbourhoods its ring map is a composite of finitely presented ring maps, so clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition] applies. For $s\in S$ and any field extension $K/\kappa(s)$, the morphism $(U_0)_s\times_{\kappa(s)}K\to X_s\times_{\kappa(s)}K$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]; its target is reduced by the hypothesis on $f$, hence its source is reduced by [etale-proposition-etale-reduced]. Thus $f\circ j$ has geometrically reduced fibres. Apply [lem-sbc-flat-reduced-etale-connected-charts] to $f\circ j$. Obtain a covering $a_i:U_i\to U_0$ with $f\circ j\circ a_i=r_i\circ q_i$, $r_i:V_i\to S$ etale, and $q_i:U_i\to V_i$ flat, quasi-compact and with nonempty geometrically connected fibres. These are precisely the charts required in unit sk-prop-deg0 Step 1. Fix one such chart and put $U=U_i$, $V=V_i$, $q=q_i$, $r=r_i$, and $j'=j\circ a_i$.

Put $G=g_*\mathcal F$, a sheaf of sets by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-continuous]. Etale inverse image is restriction by [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-restriction], so $G(V)=\Gamma(V,r^{-1}G)$ and $(f^{-1}G)(U)=\Gamma(U,(j')^{-1}f^{-1}G)$. The composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] identify $(j')^{-1}f^{-1}G$ with $q^{-1}r^{-1}G$, since $f\circ j'=r\circ q$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-sections-flat-qc-connected-fibres] to $q$ and the sheaf $r^{-1}G$: all three hypotheses were supplied by Step 1. Its canonical pullback bijection, together with these restriction and composition isomorphisms, gives a bijection $A:G(V)\xrightarrow{\sim}(f^{-1}G)(U)$. Unit compatibility in the two comparison nodes says that $A(s)$ is the unit for $f$ applied to $s$, then restricted along the chart map $U\to V\times_SX$. Lean implementation: setRestriction is explicitly constructed by uniqueness of the inverse-image and localization-restriction left adjoints; setComp is the conjugate of lowerStarComp. Private restriction_unit and composition_unit prove their unit equations. setChartSections_objectComparison combines these comparisons into a commutative square of section maps, and isIso_setSectionsMap applies the stated connected-fibre sections theorem to the terminal-object unit. These are proved set-valued counterparts of EtaleChartSectionsObjectComparison, without module coefficients.

Set $V_T=V\times_ST$, $U_T=U\times_XY\cong U\times_ST$, and let $q_T:U_T\to V_T$ be induced by $q$ and the map to $T$. The fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $U_T$ with $U\times_VV_T$ over $V_T$, so $q_T$ is a base change of $q$. It is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and quasi-compact by [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change]. For a point $v'\in V_T$ with image $v\in V$, its fibre after a field extension $K/\kappa(v')$ is $U_v\times_{\kappa(v)}K$, by the same universal property. This is nonempty and connected by the definition of geometrically connected in [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], applied to the field extension $K/\kappa(v)$. Thus $q_T$ meets all the hypotheses of the sections theorem.

The base-change functor sends etale objects to etale objects by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits], so $V_T$ and $U_T$ are etale objects over $T$ and $Y$, respectively. Write $r_T:V_T\to T$ and $j_T:U_T\to Y$ for the structure maps. Restriction [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-restriction] gives $\mathcal F(V_T)=\Gamma(V_T,r_T^{-1}\mathcal F)$ and $(e^{-1}\mathcal F)(U_T)=\Gamma(U_T,j_T^{-1}e^{-1}\mathcal F)$. Since $e\circ j_T=r_T\circ q_T$, composition [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] identifies $j_T^{-1}e^{-1}\mathcal F$ with $q_T^{-1}r_T^{-1}\mathcal F$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-sections-flat-qc-connected-fibres] to $q_T$ and $r_T^{-1}\mathcal F$, with the hypotheses checked in Step 3. Its canonical pullback bijection, followed by the composition and restriction isomorphisms, gives $B:\mathcal F(V_T)\xrightarrow{\sim}(e^{-1}\mathcal F)(U_T)$. The direct-image formula of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-continuous] identifies $G(V)=\mathcal F(V_T)$ and $(h_*e^{-1}\mathcal F)(U)=(e^{-1}\mathcal F)(U_T)$. Under these identifications $\beta_{\mathcal F}(U)\circ A=B$: for $s\in\mathcal F(V_T)$, $A(s)$ is the chart restriction of the $f$-unit, and the defining adjoint-transpose equation for $\beta$ sends that unit to the $e$-unit; restriction sends it to the pullback of $s$ on $U_T$. The restriction and composite-unit equations of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units], and the restriction-unit equation of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-restriction], identify this last section with $B(s)$. Hence $\beta_{\mathcal F}(U)=B\circ A^{-1}$ is bijective on every good chart. This checks the actual canonical morphism, not just its source and target section sets. The private setSectionsMap_comp_exchange proves this equation directly from the homEquiv apply-symm identity for setUpperLowerAdjunction and the definition of setBaseChangeArrow. Evaluating lowerStarComp reduces the rest to pullback projection equations; isPullback_pullbackFst_of_hom proves the required pasting square.

Write $H=f^{-1}g_*\mathcal F$ and $K=h_*e^{-1}\mathcal F$. They are sheaves by the inverse-image construction and direct-image theorem. First $\beta(U_0)$ is injective for every object: equal images imply equal restrictions on its good-chart cover by Step 4, and the separatedness part of the sheaf axiom gives equality. Next let $t\in K(U_0)$. On a good-chart cover let $s_i\in H(U_i)$ be its unique lifts. On $U_i\times_{U_0}U_j$ the restrictions of $s_i$ and $s_j$ have the same image, and the injectivity just proved for every object makes them equal (the overlap itself need not be a good chart). The equalizer sheaf axiom [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] glues the $s_i$ to $s\in H(U_0)$; separatedness of $K$ gives $\beta(s)=t$. Thus all components of $\beta$ are bijective. Their inverses are natural, since the original components commute with restrictions; they define an inverse sheaf morphism. In Lean this argument is the existing proved Sheaf.isIso_of_isIso_app_of_generate_mem, applied with the identity functor on sets and the Presieve.ofArrows of the connected charts. It requires invertibility only at the chart objects, so does not assume the overlaps are themselves connected charts.

If $f$ is smooth, [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion] supplies flatness and local finite presentation, and [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced] supplies geometrically reduced fibres. Steps 1--5 therefore apply without any hypothesis on $g$ or torsion assumption on $\mathcal F$, giving the smooth special case in the statement.

blueprint_update.statement:
Consider a base-change square
where $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation with
geometrically reduced
fibres (in particular, $f$ may be smooth). Then

$$
f^{-1}g_*\mathcal F=h_*e^{-1}\mathcal F
$$

for any sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $T_{\Et}$.

proof.text:
The direct image of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is computed by the
equalizer description of sections along the fibres; for a flat
morphism of finite presentation with geometrically reduced fibres, the
(reduced) connected components of the fibres are the geometric points,
and they correspond under base change, so for $V\to T$ etale the
sections of both sides over $V$ are the same systems of sections on the
fibres of $V\times_TY\to V$: this identifies $f^{-1}g_*\mathcal F$ and
$h_*e^{-1}\mathcal F$ as sheaves, which is the displayed equality.
